documents.title: The scale-free verdict reverses; the narrow window wins
documents.source_line: ** [`rh27b.html`](../rh27b.html) — §3 "Comparing eigenvalues across supports, honestly" and "The verdict, and it goes the other way"
header: **Source:** [`rh27b.html`](../rh27b.html) — §3 "Comparing eigenvalues across supports, honestly" and "The verdict, and it goes the other way"

> λ<sub>min</sub> is homogeneous in the window's normalisation, so its raw value at two different supports is not a comparison of anything. The scale to divide by is C<sub>h</sub>(0), the kernel's own diagonal — and it can be taken out exactly, because the *window family* is scale-free: C<sub>h</sub>(0)/Δ′ depends on θ alone, and the same shape at three widths gives the same number to eleven figures. At θ = 0, where the generator is the triangle, that number is 2/3 exactly. So λ<sub>min</sub>/C<sub>h</sub>(0) is the quantity to compare, and it is a genuine comparison.

> λ<sub>min</sub>/C<sub>h</sub>(0) is 1.069 at Δ′ = 0.12, 0.360 at 0.24 and 0.104 at 0.48 — a factor 10.3 in favour of the narrow window. rh21's conclusion was that Δ = 0.24 was a reasonable stopping point on the way *up* in support; nothing in rh21 argued that going *down* was bad, and it turns out that going down is where the eigenvalue is.

documents.title: The cancellation, and why there is no L¹ symbol
documents.source_line: ** [`rh28.html`](../rh28.html) — §5 "The cancellation, and why there is no symbol"
header: **Source:** [`rh28.html`](../rh28.html) — §5 "The cancellation, and why there is no symbol"

> The kernel row is pole + arch − comb. The pole carries 2ĥ(i/2)²cosh(v/2) and rises by cosh 9 = 4,052 from v = 0 to v = 18. The comb carries the gear mass Σ<sub>|ln m − v| ≤ 2Δ′</sub>Λ(m)m<sup>−½</sup>, which by the prime number theorem also rises like e<sup>v/2</sup>, and it does: at v = 18 the two agree to 0.8%. The archimedean term has decayed to 3.5×10⁻⁸ by then and is irrelevant. What is left is the row, and **the row does not grow**: its largest entry over the whole eighteen is the diagonal itself, and at v = 18 it is 7.6×10⁻³ of the pole term that made it.

> That is the explicit formula's own balance, seen directly rather than inferred. It is also the answer to the symbol question. Individually the two series diverge; the row is their difference and is bounded but not obviously summable, and the comb's lumpiness — comb/pole is 5.30 at v = 3 and 0.77 at v = 6, one prime power at a time — is what a Fourier series would have to absorb. So there is no L¹ symbol to take an infimum of, and the Szegő route to the depth infinity is closed. The arc works at finite depth because that is the only place the objects exist.

documents.title: (d) The depth, and it is not a power law
documents.source_line: ** [`rh28.html`](../rh28.html) — §6 "The depth, and it is not a power law"
header: **Source:** [`rh28.html`](../rh28.html) — §6 "The depth, and it is not a power law"

> End to end the decay is a factor 3.4 at Δ′ = 0.12 over a factor 18.8 in depth, which as a single exponent is v<sup>−0.414</sup>; across the five supports the endpoint secants are 0.972, 0.703, 0.414, 0.440, 0.394. Taken at face value that would be reassuring — a power below 1 never reaches zero — and it is the first quantitative statement the arc has about the one direction the conjunction requires infinitely much of.

> **It is not a power law, and the direction of the error matters.** The curves in Figure 4 are not straight. At Δ′ = 0.12 the local slope over the six segments runs 0.04, 0.45, 0.49, 0.52, 0.73, 0.77 — nearly flat where the section is shallow and steepening throughout, by a factor of 18 end to end. The same happens at every support. So the endpoint secant is not an exponent, it is an average dominated by the shallow segments where almost nothing is happening, and the decay past v = 18 is *steeper* than the secant, not equal to it. An extrapolation built on 0.414 is therefore optimistic, and the extrapolated costs — 2.0 to reach v = 100, 5.3 to reach 1000 — are lower bounds on what it would actually cost, not estimates.

header: **Status:** VERIFIED (numerical; composed prediction reproduces the death curve to 6.2% over five decades)
**Source:** [`rh32.html`](../rh32.html) — §4 "The death of the constant", lines 581–623 and boxed statements at lines 589–593 and 598–606

> rh31's conjecture compares λ<sub>min</sub> with the emptiest-arc ceiling C<sub>n</sub>. On the punctured crystal the ceiling is also one integral: centred mid-void, the Fejér translate sees only the two tails that leak past the void edges, and the tail integral gives
> C<sub>n</sub> ≈ (2/π<sup>2</sup>)·mass/K = 0.2026·mass/K,   measured to 6.2% for all K ≥ 2 (the residual is the sinc<sup>2</sup> tail's own oscillation about its mean).

documents.title: The crystal is not fragile: no Kadec threshold
header: > Before attacking the lemma it is worth knowing whether the crystal's exactness is a knife edge. Jitter each atom independently by up to α of a spacing and measure ρ. The classical expectation is Kadec's quarter — perturb a lattice by less than a quarter of its spacing and the exponentials stay a Riesz basis; beyond it, no guarantee.

> Nothing happens at a quarter. ρ falls in a straight line from 1, reaching 0.978 at α = ¼ and 0.957 at α = 0.49, where neighbouring atoms are nearly on top of each other, and the fall is linear to 0.3% of the total loss across the whole range. Three seeds agree to 0.0021. A destroyed lattice costs 4.3% of the constant.

documents.source_line: ** [`rh33.html`](../rh33.html) — §2 "The loss constant", lines 364–386 and boxed statement at lines 372–377
header: **Status:** VERIFIED (numerical; agrees with rh32's stored numbers at K = 1.5, 2.1, 3.1 "to the last bit")
**Source:** [`rh33.html`](../rh33.html) — §2 "The loss constant", lines 364–386 and boxed statement at lines 372–377

> Fix a mirrored atomic measure μ — atoms at ±t<sub>j</sub> with weights w<sub>j</sub> — and a degree n. Its Toeplitz matrix is T<sub>n</sub>[j][k] = E(j − k) with E(k) = ∑<sub>j</sub> w<sub>j</sub> e<sup>ikt<sub>j</sub></sup> summed over all atoms, and the number this document is about is

> ρ(μ) = λ<sub>min</sub>(T<sub>n</sub>) / mass = the largest c with ∑<sub>j</sub> w<sub>j</sub> |p(t<sub>j</sub>)|<sup>2</sup> ≥ c · mass · ‖p‖<sup>2</sup> for every trigonometric polynomial p of degree < n.

documents.title: The loss is a cancellation across the whole comb
documents.source_line: ** [`rh33.html`](../rh33.html) — §6 "The moments are a prime sum", lines 879–886
header: **Source:** [`rh33.html`](../rh33.html) — §6 "The moments are a prime sum", lines 879–886

> The tempting next sentence — *so a handful of primes decides the certificate* — is false, and the right panel is the disproof. Switch the comb off entirely and the row still has ρ = 0.762, the archimedean part alone. The twenty heaviest prime powers carry it *past* the truth, down to 0.458. The next sixty bring it back to 0.524. The loss is a cancellation across the whole comb, in the same way §5 found the moments cancelling — which is the same phenomenon seen twice, since the moments are the comb.
- The comb is the prime-power sum ∑<sub>m≥2</sub> Λ(m)·m<sup>−1/2</sup>[C<sub>h</sub>(ln m − v) + C<sub>h</sub>(ln m + v)] of [rh33-moments-are-a-prime-sum](rh33-moments-are-a-prime-sum.md).

documents.title: The counterexample needs the alias: a modulation has nowhere to stand unwrapped
header: > It bought something else. rh33 killed the quadrature lemma by modulating the weights at frequency n−1 in the *wrapped angle*: on the crystal that gives ρ = 1 − ε/2 exactly, driving the constant from 1 to 0.550 at ε = 0.9. The modulation could be placed at any frequency, because the fold makes every frequency below n available.

> Unwrapped, it has nowhere to stand. Apply the same ε = 0.9 modulation to the measure itself — W → W(1 + ε cos(v<sub>0</sub>γ)) — and the worst it achieves is a factor 0.707, at v<sub>0</sub> = log 2. The other gear rates cost between 8% and 29%. The four non-gear frequencies tried cost as little as 4.3%.

> The mechanism is not subtle: the only frequencies that couple to G are its own sampling points, and those are the gears. A modulation at a frequency that is not some log m has nothing to resonate with. rh33's counterexample was not a fact about atomic measures; **it was a fact about aliasing**, and it needed the fold to exist.
